title: Are online degrees taken seriously?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: I'm thinking about doing the master's online. Same university, same certificate, half the cost, and I don't have to leave my job.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Does the certificate actually say online on it?

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: No. That's the point. It's identical.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Then honestly, for hiring, I don't think anyone can tell and I don't think anyone asks. I've sat on panels. Nobody has ever said where the lectures were watched.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'd push back a bit there. It's not the paper, it's what you come out with. Half of what I got from mine was three years of arguing with people in a corridor after the seminar.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: There are discussion boards for that.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: There are, and they're not the same and you know they're not the same.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: That's a real difference, I'll give you that. Although a lot of campus students skip the seminars anyway and just watch the recordings.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Which is its own problem, yes.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: The honest answer for me is that the alternative isn't a campus degree. It's no degree, because I can't afford to stop earning for two years.

turns.speaker: Ravi
turns.text: Right, and that's the comparison that actually matters. Not online versus ideal. Online versus nothing.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Fine, that lands. I'd still make sure it's a real university with real supervisors, though, not a login and a video library.

points: Nina is considering an online master's from the same university: identical certificate, about half the cost, and she keeps her job.
Ravi, who has sat on hiring panels, says employers cannot tell and do not ask whether a degree was taken online.
Claire argues the value is not the certificate but the experience, citing arguments with peers after seminars, which discussion boards do not replicate.
Ravi concedes the point but notes many campus students skip seminars and watch recordings anyway.
Nina reframes the comparison: her real alternative is no degree at all, because she cannot stop earning for two years.
Claire accepts that, but advises checking it is a genuine university with real supervision rather than only a video library.
